papers.title: Remarks on Fourier--Mukai invariances
papers.abstract: This note proves that smoothness and Gorensteinness are Fourier--Mukai invariants for proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. Moreover, a kernel realizing such a partnership is perfect if, and only if, the families are smooth.

papers.title: A general theorem on the analytic spread and associated primes of divisorial filtrations
papers.abstract: We prove that a classical theorem of McAdam about the analytic spread of an ideal in a Noetherian local ring $R$ is true for rational divisorial filtrations on an arbitrary Noetherian local ring. We deduce McAdam's original theorem from our result. This generalizes earlier work by the author, showing that this theorem is true for rational divisorial filtrations, with the restriction that $R$ is an equidimensional local ring which is essentially of finite type over an excellent local ring of dimension $\le 3$.

papers.title: Gorenstein linkage of ideals and doubly layered filtrations of MCM modules
papers.abstract: The glicci conjecture asks whether every Cohen-Macaulay ideal in a regular ring belongs to the Gorenstein linkage class of a complete intersection. We show that the corresponding statement is false for nonregular rings. We prove that the conjecture holds for zero-dimensional ideals and for ideals of dimensions one and two in polynomial rings. Geometrically, this implies that every zero-dimensional subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n_k$, as well as every curve in $\mathbb{P}^n_k$, is glicci. We also prove that every Cohen-Macaulay monomial ideal is glicci. Our approach involves reducing the problem to height-two ideals and studying their N-type resolutions and the filtrations of the associated modules. We also show that every orientable maximal Cohen-Macaulay module over a two-dimensional Gorenstein ring is stably isomorphic to a doubly layered module. Finally, we prove that every ideal belongs to the Gorenstein linkage class of a Golod ideal.

papers.title: Morse resolutions and applications to lcm powers
papers.abstract: We consider the $r$-th lcm power $I^{\{r\}}$ of a monomial ideal $I$, defined to be generated by the least common multiples of all $r$-element subsets of the set of minimal monomial generators of $I$. Some homological invariants of these ideals are studied. Specifically, we use discrete Morse theory to give sharp upper bounds for the projective dimension and total Betti numbers of these ideals. Moreover, we completely determine the extent to which lcm powers define the homological shift ideals of edge ideals. Finally, we study when the minimal resolution of some ordinary powers and lcm powers are supported on the same CW-complex.

papers.title: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria
papers.abstract: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece. This relationship was anticipated by Bhatt and Mathew.

papers.title: Distance algebras of finite distributive lattices are Gorenstein
papers.abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology of quasi-metric spaces as Tor- and Ext-groups respectively. Let $\Sigma_L$ be the distance algebra of the Hasse graph of a finite distributive lattice $L$, where the metric is given by the lengths of shortest paths in the graph. We show that $\Sigma_L$ is Gorenstein over any Gorenstein commutative noetherian ring $R$, and give bound of its self-injective dimension. The proof constructs, for each indecomposable (relative) injective module, a projective resolution that is in general non-minimal. When $R=\Bbbk$ is a field, we use algebraic Morse theory to reduce it to a minimal resolution, so that the Betti numbers can be obtained as the dimensions of homologies of certain order complexes. As a consequence, we show that the self-injective dimension of $\Sigma_L$ is the maximal Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of certain Stanley--Reisner rings. We also show that the first two terms of these minimal resolutions are multiplicity-free, whereas arbitrarily large multiplicities occur in every higher degree. In the appendix, we include a more abstract formulation of the non-minimal projective resolution, namely, a simplicial replacement of a diagram of projective modules.

papers.title: Nonlinear syzygies in ordinary powers of chordal cover ideals
papers.abstract: We construct connected chordal graphs whose cover ideals have ordinary powers that are not componentwise linear over any field, disproving the Herzog--Hibi--Ohsugi conjecture.

papers.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

papers.title: New necessary conditions on $h$-vectors of simplicial balls
papers.abstract: Although the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of dimension at most $4$ have been completely characterized, much less is known in dimensions $5$ and higher. We establish new necessary conditions on the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls in these dimensions. Together with the necessary conditions of Billera and Lee and the sufficient conditions of Kolins, our results yield a complete characterization of the $h$-vectors of $5$- and $6$-dimensional simplicial balls. We also give a characterization of $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of any dimension with neighborly boundary.

papers.title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
papers.abstract: We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent. We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

papers.title: Plane partitions and spin adapted quantum states
papers.abstract: We describe an explicit basis for the $\operatorname{SU}(2)$-invariant space of the exterior power $\wedge_{2k} \mathbb{C}^{2m}$ via the combinatorics of plane partitions. In quantum chemistry, this is the space of spin adapted quantum states of an electronic system with $m$ spin orbitals and $k$ electron pairs. We construct our basis by identifying the invariant space with an Artinian commutative ring called the excitation ring. We compute a Gr\"obner basis and enumerate its standard monomials via an explicit bijection to Dyck paths counted by the Narayana numbers.

papers.title: The Betti Numbers of Kunz-Waldi Semigroups
papers.abstract: Given two coprime numbers $p<q$, KW semigroups contain $p,q$ and are contained in $\langle p,q,r \rangle$ where $2r= p,q, p+q$ whichever is even. These semigroups were first introduced by Kunz and Waldi. Kunz and Waldi proved that all $KW$ semigroups of embedding dimension $n\geq 4$ have Cohen-Macaulay type $n-1$ and first Betti number ${n \choose 2}$. In this paper, we characterize KW semigroups whose defining ideal is generated by the $2\times 2$ minors of a $2\times n$ matrix. In addition, we identify all KW semigroups that lie on the interior of the same face of the Kunz cone $\mathcal C_p$ as a KW semigroup with determinantal defining ideal. Thus, we provide an explicit formula for the Betti numbers of all those KW semigroups.

papers.title: Jordan types for pairs of commuting nilpotent matrices: A survey
papers.abstract: The aim of the paper is to survey results on Jordan types for pairs of nilpotent commuting matrices. We also review recent proof of the Box Conjecture on Jordan types that have equal dense orbit in the nilpotent commutator.

papers.title: Homology of non-matching complexes under edge additions and applications to their Stanley-Reisner ideals
papers.abstract: For a bipartite graph $G$ and an integer $t\geq 2$, we study the $t$-non-matching complex $\NM_t(G)$ and its Stanley-Reisner ideal. We prove that, if adding an edge $e$ to $G$ preserves bipartiteness, the inclusion $\NM_t(G)\hookrightarrow\NM_t(G+e)$ induces an injection on reduced homology in degree $2t-3$. If $G$ contains a cycle of length at least $2t$, then $\NM_t(G)$ has Leray number $2t-2$, and its Stanley-Reisner ideal has regularity $2t-1$. We also obtain explicit lower bounds for certain graded Betti numbers and the projective dimension of this ideal. If $G$ contains a $2t$-cycle, we determine the maximal shifts of this ideal through homological degree $|E(G)|-2t+1$. For the complete bipartite graph $G=K_{r, s}$ with $2\leq t\leq r\leq s$, we determine the depth, projective dimension, all maximal shifts, and the unique extremal Betti number of the associated ideal, thereby settling a conjecture on facet ideals of chessboard complexes.

papers.title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $\delta_i(g)=X_i$ and $\delta^\alpha(g)=(\partial^\alpha h^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $\delta^\alpha(g)=0$ for $|\alpha|=(\deg h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $\delta^\alpha(g)(x_0)/\alpha!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.
